statement: One US dollar is 49.25 Philippine pesos.
why: Average market rate for 2021, the price year of the crop cost data.
sensitivity: Already the house convention. Changing it would break comparability with the rice VariableCost already stored in the case.

statement: Crop VariableCost = output activity ratio (Mt per 10^3 km2) x production cost (PHP/kg) x 1000 kg/t / 49.25 PHP/USD.
why: This is the formula already used for the two rice modes in the case.
sensitivity: Verified: 0.32229806503462954 x 13.95 x 20.30456852791878 = 91.29051791336207, the stored value for LNDAGRPHLC01 mode 11. Matches CALC_PHL_V16_CROP_RICE_VARIABLE_COST in the canonical ledger.

statement: For crops other than palay, production cost per kilogram is the 2021 farmgate unit value times palay's own cost-to-unit-value ratio: 0.749175 irrigated, 0.836761 rainfed.
why: PSA runs a cost-and-returns survey for palay only. No Philippine source publishes cost per kilogram for maize, coconut, sugarcane, tomato or the residual crop group.
sensitivity: This is the single largest judgement in the crop block: it assumes every crop spends the same share of its farmgate value on production. The 2022 total-cost-to-gross-returns ratios from Tables 5.6 and 5.7 (0.8172 irrigated, 0.8832 rainfed) are an alternative, and substituting them raises every non-rice crop cost by 9 percent irrigated and 6 percent rainfed.

statement: Road-vehicle maintenance cost per kilometre is 1.8462e-06 times the price of a new vehicle.
why: Derived from an observed Philippine bus operator cost and corroborated by the Philippine HDM-4 calibration.
sensitivity: PIDS gives 1.8462e-06 per km including maintenance labour; MMUTIS gives 1.82e-06 per km for parts alone. The 1.4 percent gap is smaller than either source's own uncertainty.

statement: The same coefficient applies to every road vehicle class, scaled by that class's capital cost.
why: HDM-4, the model family MMUTIS calibrated, expresses parts consumption as a percentage of new-vehicle price for every vehicle class.
sensitivity: Weakest for two- and three-wheelers, whose maintenance does not fall linearly with price: the resulting 0.0016 USD/km is at the low end of plausibility. Those three proposals are marked LOW confidence.

statement: Road transport activity in this case is vehicle-kilometres, not passenger- or tonne-kilometres, despite the commodity names.
why: Every road technology has an output activity ratio of exactly 1, and the input activity ratios are per-vehicle fuel intensities: 1.449 MJ/km for a car, about 4.5 L/100 km, and 9.92 MJ/km for a bus, about 27.5 L/100 km.
sensitivity: If passenger-kilometres were intended, every proposal here would have to be divided by an occupancy factor.

statement: Plug-in hybrid VariableCost is the mean of the same-class internal-combustion and battery-electric proposals, not a value scaled from its own capital cost.
why: The stored plug-in hybrid capital costs are about 1000 times too large: car 14000, bus 75000, heavy truck 57000, light truck and van 18000 MUSD per 10^3 vehicles. Any capex-proportional rule would inherit that error.
sensitivity: Recompute these five proposals once the capital costs are corrected.

statement: United States variable operations and maintenance costs are used for Philippine power plants.
why: No Philippine institution publishes technology-level non-fuel variable operating cost. The closest national data, the PSA Annual Survey of Philippine Business and Industry, implies about 51 USD/MWh of non-intermediate expense for the electricity sector, which plainly includes depreciation, taxes, interest and distribution margin and so cannot be used as variable O&M.
sensitivity: Variable O&M is dominated by consumables and wear-related overhaul, both internationally traded; the labour share, where the Philippines differs most, sits mainly in fixed O&M. Expect true Philippine values somewhat below these.

statement: For a technology whose activity unit is PJ, VariableCost in MUSD per PJ is numerically USD per GJ.
sensitivity: This is why the conversion from USD/MWh is a division by 3.6.

statement: Biomass with carbon capture costs the biomass variable O&M plus the increment capture adds to coal, 12.35 minus 5.06 = 7.29 2022USD/MWh.
why: The EIA table has no biomass-with-capture row.
sensitivity: Marked LOW confidence. The increment is dominated by solvent make-up and CO2 compression, which scale with captured CO2, and biomass flue gas differs from coal flue gas.
